import { defineTable, col, rel } from "@rebasepro/server/schema";
import { customer } from "./customer";
import { invoiceLine } from "./invoice_line";

// ⚠ Not reproduced exactly by `rebase db push` — read before pushing:
//   - "invoice_date" is timestamp without time zone, declared with `col.custom()`: Rebase serves it as the driver returns it, and `rebase db generate` / `db push` refuse it until the planner can plan a custom type (`custom-sql-type`).
export const invoice = defineTable("invoice", {
    columns: {
        invoiceId: col.integer().primaryKey(),
        customerId: col.integer().notNull(),
        invoiceDate: col.custom("timestamp without time zone").notNull(),
        billingAddress: col.varchar(70),
        billingCity: col.varchar(40),
        billingState: col.varchar(40),
        billingCountry: col.varchar(40),
        billingPostalCode: col.varchar(10),
        total: col.numeric(10, 2).notNull()
    },
    relations: {
        customer: rel.belongsTo(() => customer, { onDelete: "no action" }),
        invoice_line: rel.hasMany(() => invoiceLine)
    },
    rls: "admin-only"
});
